chapter: West Coast trip and Mildred's circle
title: Mildred Bailey's brothers Chuck and Miles Rinker
summary: Al Rinker is Mildred's brother; Norvo describes brother Chuck Rinker, a song plugger, and meeting Miles Rinker, a saxophonist, without knowing he was Mildred's brother.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, I see Al all the time. But I see Chuck, there's another brother, Mildred 's other brother, and she had a brother.
What does Chuck do?

Well Chuck she brought in New York, didn't you meet him, he used to work, Mildred brought him in from California, he had a -- he had a trio with Bob Crosby and ah -- oh, what's his name, I can't remember his name now, he was married to Lorraine Day for awhile, he was a pilot, he's an Alaskan pibt now, I understand. But they had a little trio in Los Angeles together.
You mean singing?
Yeah, singing. And then Mildred (unintelligible).
brought him to New York when we were in Forest Hills.
I don't remember that.
Yeah, he was a song plugger for Irving Berlin.
Really?
He was the one that kind of started that group that was with Glen Miller, what's the singing group -- Paula Kelly and --
Yeah, I know, I remember that.

Well they started up -- they rehearsed up at his place. And he was with Irving -- I mean Irving Berlin Music Company for a long while -- oh, yeah, he was around here for a long while. I thought you knew him.
No --
Chuck Rinker.
No, I didn't. Isn't that funny I never realized that.

And I met Mildred's older brother, Miles at the University of Illinois. When I went back, later, about three years later, -- two years later, I think, I went back and played the Orpheum Theater in Champagne and Miles was working a band, he was a saxophone player. He was very good with oh, some very good players, Larry Binyon was in the band, you remember him?
For heaven's sake, yeah, vaguely. Yeah.
Used to play with a duo do that work around New York --
Yeah.
Snub Pollard, a wonderful trumpet player became a lawyer and a doctor, now --
I'll be darned.
Some great musicians and I knew Miles and never realized he was Mildred's brother. After I knew Mildred, till I -- till I went to the coast and we recognized each other.
How funny.
After -- in 1930 -- wait a minute, '37, when Mildred and I went to the coast we recognized each other.
